lines.text: He drops rusty nuts into 7 rust removers including Coke and vinegar to see which one eats rust fastest.
Evapo-Rust is the odd one because it's pH neutral so it's sold as super safe.
It uses chelation where big molecules grab the iron like tiny claws and hold it in the liquid.
beats: ai:orange rust flakes lifting off a steel nut into clear amber liquid macro photo
ai:a tiny mechanical claw gripping an orange rust particle underwater macro

lines.text: But Krud Kutter turns its nuts grey in 5 hours while Evapo-Rust barely changes after the first hour.
Muriatic acid cleans best by far and takes its nuts down to bare shiny steel.
But it's 31 percent hydrochloric acid so it eats good metal too and you lose steel along with the rust.
beats: ai:steel bolt fizzing with tiny bubbles in clear acid macro

lines.text: After 24 hours the Krud Kutter bolt looks amazing but Evapo-Rust still leaves rust in the threads.
And on sheet metal Evapo-Rust barely works because it needs a full soak and a wet paper towel isn't enough.
beats: ai:a rusty wrench fully submerged in a plastic tub of amber liquid

lines.text: So Krud Kutter wins and 23 hours in it makes this rusty wrench look almost new.
But it's the priciest at 62 cents an ounce and he says Evapo-Rust comes very close and you can reuse it.
So which one would you trust on your tools?
